protections: HMAC algorithms must refuse asymmetric key material used as the HMAC secret (the HS/asymmetric-confusion guard); in the pinned code this is the four-literal denylist inside HMACAlgorithm.prepare_key (jwt/algorithms.py:183-199).

traps.reason_to_dismiss: Only ssh-rsa is listed and the RSA section documents 'PEM or SSH format' while the ECDSA section documents PEM only (docs/algorithms.rst:29-36), so the SSH surface looks covered; an OpenSSH EC or Ed25519 public-key string does not look like a key this guard is meant to see.

These are private-key PEM labels: an attacker who does not know the private key cannot produce the matching HMAC, and the report's own whitespace/CRLF variants of a '-----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----' header still contain the literal matched at jwt/algorithms.py:193, so the stated repro does not reproduce.

kty=oct is a symmetric key by definition and a JWKS is fetched from a trusted issuer, so an attacker cannot place PEM bytes there; the documented PyJWKClient flow re-passes jwk.key into jwt.decode (docs/usage.rst:291-297), where prepare_key still runs.

prepare_key-then-sign/verify is the class contract, jwt.algorithms is not part of the documented API, and PyJWT's own decode path always prepares the key first (jwt/api_jws.py:264-268); no attacker decides whether these methods are called directly.

fairness_risks: Arbitrary symmetric secrets must keep working: the current guard rejects only three exact PEM banners and the ssh-rsa literal (jwt/algorithms.py:186-191), so any widened rule that rejects keys merely containing '-----BEGIN' or starting with 'ssh-' changes behaviour for legitimate HMAC secrets.

Rejecting OpenSSH 'ecdsa-sha2-*' and 'ssh-ed25519' strings as HMAC secrets must not affect their use as ES256/EdDSA verification keys: the same text is deliberately accepted by ECAlgorithm.prepare_key (jwt/algorithms.py:413) and OKPAlgorithm.prepare_key (jwt/algorithms.py:570).

Private PEM keys must remain accepted by the asymmetric prepare_key paths (jwt/algorithms.py:262, 416-418, 568); a global PEM ban would break RS/ES/EdDSA verification, so the refusal has to stay scoped to the HMAC branch.

The shapes the report names (whitespace/CRLF-mutated '-----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----' headers) are already rejected by the substring test at jwt/algorithms.py:193, so a test set built only from that description would pass before any fix and would not exercise the real gaps.

design.why: Only two independent guard sites exist. The prepare_key denylist (T1/T2) is one guard: a single rewritten detector closes both the missing OpenSSH EC/Ed25519 shapes and the missing PEM labels, so they count once; T1 is the representative because it is the attacker-reachable shape (a public key the library itself accepts for ES256/EdDSA at jwt/algorithms.py:413 and :570), while T2's stronger excuse (private-key labels; the report's whitespace repro does not reproduce) cannot be counted separately. The second group is the unguarded HMAC sink: a check inside sign/verify closes both the from_jwk route (T3) and direct sign/verify calls (T4), so those count once; T3 is the representative because the JWK producer chain (jwt/api_jwk.py:52, jwt/jwks_client.py:25-38) carries a different excuse from T1's. Two groups are below the 3-5 independent-trap bar, and the second group is not reachable through PyJWT's documented decode path (docs/usage.rst:291-297 re-runs prepare_key), so this candidate does not support a stacked task.

unverified: The published fix commit 8b4e233a2220 is not in this worktree (HEAD is 24b29ad), so which of T3/T4 the fix touches cannot be checked; only T1/T2 are demonstrably on the check named by the advisory.

PyJWKClient resolves the signing key from the unverified kid header (jwt/jwks_client.py:56-59); that is a key-selection concern outside this advisory's HMAC/asymmetric guard and is not counted as a trap.

The report's 'PEM detection' framing may cover a broader detector rewrite (e.g. a generic '-----BEGIN [A-Z0-9 ]+-----' matcher plus an SSH-prefix tuple); if so, T1/T2 are the same single fix and the stack is one independent trap.
